findings.defect: The rule only fires when the conversion TARGET's underlying type is a pointer. For a type parameter P the underlying type is its constraint interface, so pointerElement(P) is false and the conversion is accepted unchecked. A constraint interface{*L} or ~*L, with L an own defined type over a foreign type, makes P(foreignPtr) legal Go; the instantiated pointee is the own named L and every subsequent write passes ownPointeeWrite. The b47 README promise 'An own defined pointee name cannot launder a foreign pointer; slice-to-array-pointer conversions are refused by this rule' is therefore false for generic targets. Same process-global utcLoc object as N1.
